nodes.label: pnpm Workspace Config
nodes.rationale: Minimal pnpm workspace configuration: ignores postinstall (`pmOnFail: ignore`), excludes `@next/*` and `next` packages from pnpm's minimum-release-age safety delay (`minimumReleaseAgeExclude`), and explicitly allows the `protobufjs` package to run native build scripts (`allowBuilds`) — the latter is notable given the plan's addition of the `firebase` SDK dependency, whose transitive dependency tree includes protobufjs.

nodes.label: Composite Index for Chats List Query
nodes.norm_label: composite index for chats list query
nodes.rationale: The conversation list query in components/chats/chats-view.tsx is the only query in the app that filters on one field (`array-contains` on participantIds) and sorts on a different field (lastMessageAt) — every other query (posts, messages, friend requests) filters/sorts on the same field and needs no composite index. Firestore will throw an error containing a console link to auto-create the exact index the first time this query runs against a real project; this is called out explicitly as normal Firestore behavior, not a bug, so it isn't pre-provisioned in code.

nodes.label: TTL Policy Enablement (gcloud/Console)
nodes.rationale: TTL can only be configured against a real, existing collection group, so enabling it (via `gcloud firestore fields ttls update expiresAt --collection-group=... --enable-ttl` or the Console equivalent) must happen after project creation and is a manual/CLI step, not something the repo's code can do. Firestore describes TTL deletion as happening 'within 24 hours' of the timestamp rather than instantly, so this step is framed as being only about eventually reclaiming storage — the app's own client-side query filter is what makes visible expiry exact.

nodes.label: Client-side Expiry Filter (moving now-tick)
nodes.rationale: Every read query (posts, messages) applies `where('expiresAt', '>', now)` in addition to relying on Firestore TTL. Crucially the `now` bound is a state value (`nowTick`) refreshed every 60s via setInterval, not captured once at mount — because Firestore's realtime listener does not re-evaluate an inequality against a moving 'now', so a document crossing its expiresAt in an open tab would otherwise keep matching the original snapshot's cutoff and linger on screen until the slow TTL sweep actually deletes it. This is the mechanism that makes visible expiry exact regardless of TTL sweep timing, per spec ruling R6.

nodes.label: Firestore Query/DocumentReference Instability Pattern
nodes.rationale: Global Constraint stated up front: Firestore JS SDK query() and doc() objects are not stable across renders, so every call site feeding useCollection/useDocument in this plan wraps the query/doc construction in useMemo keyed on the primitive values it depends on (never the auth/profile object itself). Applies uniformly to postsQuery, conversationsQuery, messagesQuery, usersQuery, outgoing/incomingQuery, and profileRef — stated once as a rule that every task must follow rather than re-derived per task.

nodes.label: Hand-rolled PWA Shell (manifest + minimal service worker)
nodes.norm_label: hand-rolled pwa shell (manifest + minimal service worker)
nodes.rationale: PWA support is a hand-rolled web app manifest plus a minimal service worker rather than the `next-pwa` package, because next-pwa is webpack-only and this project builds with Turbopack. The service worker itself uses a network-first fetch strategy (falling back to the cached app shell only when the network fails) so residents always see live posts/messages when online — explicitly scoped to app-shell caching only, no push notifications or background sync, per the spec's Out of Scope ruling.

nodes.label: Conversations participantIds Immutability
nodes.rationale: firestore.rules forbids any update to a conversation document that changes its participantIds array after creation. Without this, either participant could rewrite participantIds to add a third party or drop the other person, retroactively exposing or locking someone out of the entire prior message history — because the messages subcollection's own rules trust the parent conversation document's *current* participantIds to decide read/write access.

nodes.label: profileRef Memoization Fix
nodes.rationale: In lib/auth-context.tsx, `doc(db, 'users', firebaseUser.uid)` is wrapped in `useMemo(..., [firebaseUser?.uid])` rather than called bare, because Firestore's doc() returns a fresh DocumentReference with no stable identity on every call. Without memoization, useDocument's `[ref]`-keyed effect would see a 'changed' ref on every render — including the re-renders its own onSnapshot callback triggers via setData — producing an infinite unsubscribe/resubscribe loop for as long as anyone is logged in, not just a wasted render.

nodes.label: Denormalized Post Author Fields
nodes.rationale: posts/{postId} stores authorName, authorProgram, authorRoom, and authorInitials directly on the post document rather than only an authorId, explicitly annotated in the data model as denormalized 'for feed rendering without N+1 reads' — avoiding a per-post lookup into the users collection just to render the feed.

nodes.label: Firestore Native TTL
nodes.rationale: R6 ruling: expiry (24h for posts/reports, 4h for messages) is implemented as Firestore's native TTL feature on an `expiresAt: Timestamp` field per collection — free, built-in, no Cloud Functions and no Blaze billing plan required — rather than a scheduled Cloud Function. Chosen specifically because it avoids the billing-plan requirement that a Cloud Function approach would reintroduce (same reasoning cited for the no-friends-array design). Because TTL deletion happens 'within 24 hours' of the timestamp rather than instantly, it is paired with a client-side query filter for exact visible behavior; TTL alone only guarantees eventual storage reclamation.

nodes.label: beforeinstallprompt Graceful Degradation
nodes.rationale: R4 requires capturing the `beforeinstallprompt` event to surface an 'Install App' action in the dashboard sidebar, but explicitly rules that browsers which never fire the event (iOS Safari, or an already-installed app) must not show a broken or dead button — the install control simply renders nothing rather than a non-functional affordance.

nodes.label: No-friends-array Design
nodes.rationale: users/{uid} deliberately has no `friends: string[]` field. Accepting a friend request would require writing the other party's uid into MY array and my uid into THEIRS in one logical operation — a cross-user write that security rules can't grant to a non-owner without either a Cloud Function (reintroducing the Blaze billing requirement R6 explicitly avoids) or an overly permissive rule letting any signed-in user edit any other user's document. Instead friendship is derived by querying `friendRequests` docs with status 'accepted' in both directions and merging client-side, keeping every write a single-document write to a doc the writer owns.

nodes.label: Remember-me Auth Persistence Toggle
nodes.rationale: R5: a 'Remember me' checkbox maps directly onto Firebase Auth's persistence modes — checked uses `browserLocalPersistence` (survives browser restart, and is the default, checked state, matching the request to 'make logins remember'); unchecked uses `browserSessionPersistence` (cleared when the tab closes).

nodes.label: Firebase Setup Guide
nodes.rationale: One-time operational runbook for wiring a real Firebase project into the app after the code side of the plan is done: register a web app, enable Email/Password auth, create Firestore in production mode, deploy firestore.rules, enable native TTL policies on posts/reports/messages, and (only the first time the chats query runs) create the composite index Firestore demands for the participantIds array-contains + lastMessageAt sort. Notably has only 6 sections and no 'promote an admin' step, unlike the 7-step version embedded in the implementation plan's Task 2 — evidence this file was revised after the plan was authored to match the later role/admin-removal decision.

nodes.label: Firebase + PWA Integration Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: 10-task, checkbox-tracked implementation plan wiring real Firebase Auth + Firestore into the Delbert boarding-house app (login, dashboard, chats, friends, requests, reports, accounts), converting it to an installable mobile-responsive PWA, and enforcing 24h post/report expiry plus 4h message expiry with matching Firestore security rules. Explicitly written for agentic execution via superpowers:subagent-driven-development or superpowers:executing-plans, task-by-task with tsc/build verification and commits per task.

nodes.label: Firebase + PWA Integration Spec
nodes.rationale: Requirements spec (R1-R7) plus Firestore data model and explicit Out-of-Scope rulings for wiring Firebase Auth/Firestore into the Delbert app, making it an installable PWA, and enforcing 24h post/report and 4h message expiry. States it is the source-of-truth referenced by the implementation plan and documents post-initial-build revisions such as removing role-based accounts/admin and making reports public and anonymous.

nodes.label: Honesty Principle: Don't Invent Data
nodes.rationale: Explicitly named in the plan's Task 4 note as 'a direct application of the Honesty principle carried over from this session's earlier graphify pass: don't invent data.' Applied concretely by dropping RightRail's fabricated 'residents online' pulse card rather than keeping fake numbers (the data model has no presence beyond a boolean), and by flagging friendRequests' raw fromUid display in RequestsView as a known rough edge rather than silently faking a resolved display name. Also underlies the decision to leave NotificationPopover's mock content clearly out of scope rather than partially wiring it to real data.

nodes.label: No Test Framework / No Live E2E Testing Ruling
nodes.norm_label: no test framework / no live e2e testing ruling
nodes.rationale: Explicit Out-of-Scope ruling: the repo has no test runner, no test files, no CI, and next.config.mjs even sets `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors: true` — standing up Jest/Vitest plus the Firebase Emulator Suite for a rapid-prototype v0-generated codebase is deemed a substantial, unrequested infrastructure project. Verification per task is `npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build` plus manual code-review read-through instead of automated tests — a deliberate deviation from the org's usual TDD default, and reviewers are told not to flag 'no tests' as a defect. Compounded by the fact no real Firebase project exists yet, so no task can be verified against a live Auth/Firestore backend either; code must fail gracefully on missing/placeholder env vars but functional correctness of the Firebase wiring itself is a code-review judgment call until real credentials are supplied.

nodes.label: Reports Become Public and Anonymous
nodes.rationale: Direct consequence of removing the role/admin model: reports are now readable by any signed-in resident (`allow read: if isSignedIn();`) rather than only their author or an admin, and are rendered anonymously in the UI — `authorId` stays in the document solely to satisfy the create rule's ownership check and is never displayed. ReportsView shows a live list of all active reports as cards styled like Freedom Wall posts beneath the submission form, not just the submitter's own, matching this public-but-anonymous model.

nodes.label: Role/Admin Model Removal
nodes.rationale: Revised after initial build per the user's explicit decision against an admin/private-reports model: 'easier to maintain, no role based accounts, everyone is a user.' `role` was removed from UserProfile and from firestore.rules, along with the `myRole()`/`isAdmin()` helper functions that had gated report visibility and admin promotion. This is an explicitly documented post-plan revision, not part of the original 10-task plan's rules as first written (which still reference role/admin in firestore.rules and the setup doc's 'promote an admin' step).
